subject: Clarify: default log retention for requests vs generated outputs
messages:
From: Laura Smith <laura.smith@acmepayments.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurements@acmepayments.com
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify: default log retention for requests vs generated outputs

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency numbers looked great. Procurement and security are working through our vendor questionnaire and we have a couple of practical questions about Redwood's default log retention that popped up from our legal team. Can you confirm the default retention windows for the following (if they're different, please call out):

- Raw request payloads (user prompts / inputs)
- Model responses / generated outputs (both final responses and streamed partial tokens)
- Any derived artifacts (embeddings, reranking scores, n-best lists)
- KV cache / session artifacts used to serve streaming / chat continuity

We also need to understand the deletion path: if we ask for erasure or when a customer account is closed, what actually gets deleted vs tombstoned and how long before permanent purge?

If you have a short matrix or a PDF we can attach to our SOC2 appendix that would be ideal.

Appreciate a quick clarifying note so we can sign off on the vendor questionnaire.

Best,
Laura
Laura Smith
Head of Security & Privacy
Acme Payments

From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Laura Smith <laura.smith@acmepayments.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: default log retention for requests vs generated outputs

Laura — thanks for the clear list. I copied Marissa (product) and Kimberly (security/compliance) so you get the policy view + operational runbook. Below is a concise summary; attaching a one‑page matrix and a short explainer PDF.

Short answers (default hosted API behavior unless a customer configures a different policy via Dedicated/Private):

- Raw request payloads (prompts / user inputs): default retention = 30 days. These are stored as request artifacts in the telemetry store and used for debugging, quality checks, and cost analytics. For customers who opt out or use Private, this can be turned off or set to a shorter TTL.

- Model responses / generated outputs (final response objects): default retention = 30 days. Generated outputs are treated as "response artifacts" and are in the same retention class as requests for hosted customers. Note: for streaming responses we persist the final response object; intermediate token fragments are not materialized as separate long‑lived artifacts beyond what is needed to continue an active stream.

- Derived artifacts (embeddings, reranks, features): default retention = 90 days for embeddings and derived artifacts generated by Redwood's Optimize/eval pipelines; embeddings created by customers via the embeddings endpoint are configurable and often set to 90 days by default in hosted tiers. If a customer chooses long‑term indexing (e.g., vector DB export), those exports are outside Redwood's hosted retention and controlled by the customer.

- KV cache / session artifacts: short‑lived, TTL tied to session activity. Default idle TTL = 24 hours; session tombstone after 30 days of inactivity to allow for debugging traces. KV entries used to speed inference are automatically pruned by the runtime; they are not indexed as long‑term logs.

Deletion / erasure path (summary):
- Customer requests for data erasure trigger an account‑wide purge workflow. For hosted customers we mark the artifacts for deletion immediately (tombstone) and start the asynchronous purge. Tombstoned items remain unavailable to queries but are kept for up to 7 days to allow incident rollback, then permanently purged.
- Complete account deletion (after customer confirmation) begins immediate tombstone and a 7‑day purge window followed by irreversible deletion from primary stores. Backups are retained per our backup retention policy (30 days) and are rotated; permanent removal from backups can take up to an additional 30 days depending on snapshot cycles.
- Note: for Dedicated and Private deployments, deletion timelines are governed by the customer's config and any on‑prem backup retention they control.

Operational notes & exceptions:
- PII flagged by automated detectors is quarantined and reviewed; we can provide an audit trail for flagged items.
- Logs referenced in support tickets may be retained longer if they're part of an open support case (we surface this in the runbook).
- Streaming token buffers are ephemeral and not captured as persistent artifacts beyond the final assembled response.

Attachments included: redwood-retention-summary-v1.pdf (short matrix) and data-retention-matrix.xlsx (detailed rows).

If it helps, Kimberly can add the exact language you should put in the SOC2 appendix (short paragraph + link).

Thanks,
Diego
Diego Fernandez
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Hi Laura — following up with the formal SOC2 wording below that you can paste into your vendor appendix. Happy to jump on a 20‑minute call if you'd like to walk through any of the timelines.

Suggested SOC2 vendor appendix language (editable):
"Redwood Inference retains customer request and response artifacts in the hosted platform for a default period of 30 days to support debugging, monitoring, and quality assurance. Derived artifacts such as embeddings and analysis artifacts are retained for a default period of 90 days. Session KV caches are ephemeral (24‑hour idle TTL) and tombstoned after 30 days of inactivity. Upon a verified customer erasure or account termination request, Redwood initiates an immediate tombstone and asynchronous purge; primary stores are purged within 7 days, with removal from incremental backups completed within the subsequent 30 days as backup cycles allow. For Dedicated or Private deployments, retention is controlled by customer configuration and contractual terms."
We've attached the two files Diego referenced. If you'd like we can provide a redline of the appendix into your vendor questionnaire and route it back via DocuSign for signature.

Cheers,
